---
title: Repository actions
---

## Overview

When a website's source lives in a public repository, Quarto can add
links that send readers straight to it — to edit the current page, to
view its source, or to file an issue:

```yaml
website:
  repo-url: https://github.com/owner/repo
  repo-actions: [edit, source, issue]
```

On a page with a table of contents, the links render twice: at the
foot of the TOC, and again in the page footer, where responsive
classes keep them visible on narrow viewports where the TOC is
hidden. On a page with no table of contents, they render once, in
the footer.

## Configuration

`repo-actions` is a list drawn from:

| action | link |
|---|---|
| `edit` | "Edit this page" — opens the source file in the host's web editor |
| `source` | "View source" — opens the source file for reading |
| `issue` | "Report an issue" — opens the issue tracker |

Use `none` to clear the list. An unrecognized entry is skipped and
reported ([`Q-13-12`](/errors/navigation/Q-13-12.qmd)); the remaining
actions still render. Setting `repo-actions: none` does not remove the
"Report an issue" link if `issue-url` is configured — that link is
controlled by `issue-url` on its own, independent of the action list.

`repo-actions` requires `repo-url` — without it, Quarto has no base
to build `edit` and `source` links from, and no default target for
`issue`. Setting `repo-actions` with no `repo-url` (and no
`issue-url`) reports [`Q-13-11`](/errors/navigation/Q-13-11.qmd) and
renders no links.

A few supporting keys, set alongside `repo-url`:

```yaml
website:
  repo-url: https://github.com/owner/repo
  repo-actions: [edit, source, issue]
  repo-branch: main
  repo-subdir: docs
  issue-url: https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/new
  repo-link-target: _blank
  repo-link-rel: noopener
```

- `repo-branch` — the branch the `edit` and `source` links point at.
  Defaults to `main`.
- `repo-subdir` — set this when the website's project lives in a
  subdirectory of its repository, so that source paths resolve
  correctly.
- `issue-url` — a custom issue tracker URL, used in place of the
  repository's default `/issues/new`. Setting `issue-url` adds a
  "Report an issue" link even if `issue` is not in `repo-actions`.
- `repo-link-target` / `repo-link-rel` — become `target=` and `rel=`
  attributes on the generated anchors.

All of these can be overridden per page in front matter — but
`repo-actions` itself cannot. In front matter, `repo-actions` is only
the `false` switch described below.

## Turning actions off for one page

Set `repo-actions: false` in a page's front matter to suppress the
links on that page only:

```yaml
---
title: My Page
repo-actions: false
---
```

## Interaction with `page-footer`

Setting `page-footer: false` — at the site or page level — suppresses
the page footer entirely, and with it the footer copy of the repo
action links. This is a deliberate divergence from Quarto 1, where the
footer copy is not tied to `page-footer`. On a page with a table of
contents, the TOC copy is unaffected and the links still appear there;
on a page with no table of contents, `page-footer: false` removes the
links from the page altogether, since the footer was their only
placement.

## Known limitations

**Page-level `repo-actions: true` is not supported.** In Quarto 1,
setting `repo-actions: true` in front matter never turned the
actions on by itself — the action list always came from the site's
`website.repo-actions` — it only requested a different *placement*
(the right margin) on a page with no table of contents. Quarto 2
does not implement that placement: the value is ignored and reported
as [`Q-13-13`](/errors/navigation/Q-13-13.qmd) (severity `info`). Nothing
is lost but the position — the links still render in the footer at
every width.

**`.ipynb` pages get no "Edit this page" link outside GitHub.** For
notebook source files, an edit link only works on `github.com`,
where Quarto rewrites it to `github.dev` so the notebook opens in an
editor rather than as rendered JSON. On any other host the edit link
is omitted for `.ipynb` pages — "View source" and "Report an issue"
are unaffected. This matches Quarto 1's behavior.
